name: Klap
summary: AI video clipper that turns long videos into vertical clips for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, with captions, reframing, scheduling and a free trial on one video.
best_for: creators, podcasters and small teams with long videos who want vertical clips with captions and reframing made automatically, and who will post often enough to use a plan of 100 to 1,000 clips a month
skip_if: you want to cut every clip by hand, you only need one or two shorts a year, you want a permanent free plan, or you want a tool we have tested through a paid plan ourselves
honest_knock: The cheap price is the yearly one: monthly billing is double, so a trial month is the costly way in. The only free try is one video, and nothing can be downloaded or posted without paying. Klap selects the clips, so the cut may not be the one you would make. We have not paid for a plan, so how it holds up over months is unknown to us.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic · per month billed yearly ($174 a year) for 100 clips a month
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on klap.app/pricing, US dollars) Three plans, each with AI clipping, captions, scheduling and analytics. Basic: 100 clips a month, $14.50 a month billed yearly ($174 a year) or $29 month to month. Pro: 300 clips, $39.50 a month billed yearly ($474 a year) or $79 monthly. Pro+: 1,000 clips, $94.50 a month billed yearly ($1,134 a year) or $189 monthly. Free trial on 1 video, no card; downloading and posting need a paid plan. API priced separately: $0.44 per input video, $0.32 per short, $0.48 per export. We have not paid for a plan.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 29 October 2026 the session tested Klap on a 30-day Pro period that Klap itself supplied, so nothing here describes the ordinary free route. We uploaded one of our own review videos (2 minutes 57 seconds, cut down to 720p so our upload tool could carry it), asked for shorts with the default settings and downloaded one clip. The Billing page showed no subscription, only a Choose a plan button; the Usage page showed 0 of 300 clips. Nothing was paid and no card was entered.
findings: Text we checked: "Generate ~7 shorts". What we saw: the dialog promised about 7 shorts; the finished run produced 4 shorts, each with a virality score between 65 and 75 out of 100, and the page showed the result less than 4 minutes after the start (09:52:40, done by 09:56:36 Dutch time).
Text we checked: "Clips 0 / 300". What we saw: the Usage page counted the run as 4 clips used of 300, so a run is billed by the clips it returns, not by the 7 it announced.

Text we checked: "Download HD". What we saw: the downloaded MP4 measured 1080 by 1920 pixels and showed no Klap watermark in the frames we inspected; the download routes we looked at offered no separate SRT, transcript or editable project file.

Text we checked: "Get $5 in free API credits". What we saw: the API page holds a separate prepaid balance of $0.00, not included in Pro, and asks for a card to unlock the free credits; we created no key and made no API call.
not_tested: The public free route, the paid checkout and when the supplied Pro period really ends.
Importing an editable project back into Klap, and the official CSV and PNG media kit.
Team roles and invitations, because the account menu offered no such screen.
Cancelling or downgrading, because the account held no subscription.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
